cards.back: Full head: an electron pair moves (polar steps, resonance). Half head (fishhook): a single electron moves (radical steps). Arrows show electrons, never atoms, and always start at a lone pair, a pi bond or a sigma bond.

cards.front: Formal-charge rule for arrow heads and tails
cards.back: Where a head lands on an atom, that atom becomes one unit more negative; where a tail leaves one, that atom becomes one unit more positive. Heads and tails may also sit on bonds, which moves charge between the two atoms they join. If a head lands on a second-period atom that already has an octet, another arrow must leave it in the same step; a third-period atom can expand its valence shell instead.
